arxiv-2203-11767.title: Weak ferromagnetism linked to the high-temperature spiral phase of YBaCuFeO 5
arxiv-2203-11767.creator: J. Lyu, M. Morin, T. Shang, M. T. Fernández-Díaz, M. Medarde
arxiv-2203-11767.description: Abstract The layered perovskite YBaCuFeO 5 is a rare example of cycloidal spiral magnet whose ordering temperature T spiral can be tuned far beyond room temperature by adjusting the degree of Cu 2+ /Fe 3+ chemical disorder in the structure. This unusual property qualifies this material as one of the most promising spin-driven multiferroic candidates.

arxiv-2409-19046.title: Subsystem entropy in 2d CFT and KdV ETH
arxiv-2409-19046.creator: Liangyu Chen, Anatoly Dymarsky, Jia Tian, and Huajia Wang
arxiv-2409-19046.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Liangyu Chen, Anatoly Dymarsky, Jia Tian, and Huajia Wang. We study subsystem entropy in 2d CFTs, for subsystems constituting a finite fraction of the full system. We focus on the extensive contribution, which scales linearly with the subsystem size in the thermodynamic limit. We employ the so-called diagonal approximation to evaluate subsystem entropy for the chaotic CFTs in thermal state (canonical ensemble), microcanonical ensemble, and in a primary state, matching previously known results.

arxiv-2410-02075.creator: Laura E. McCann, Jeffrey D. Michler, Maybin Mwangala, Osaretin Olurotimi, Natalia Estrada Carmona
arxiv-2410-02075.description: Abstract Population pressure is speeding the rate of deforestation in Sub-Saharan Africa, increasing the cost of biomass cooking fuel, which over 80% of the population relies upon. Higher energy input costs for meal preparation command a larger portion of household spending which in turn induces families to focus their diet on quick cooking staples.

arxiv-2411-06971.title: MapSAM: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Automated Feature Detection in Historical Maps
arxiv-2411-06971.creator: Xue Xia, Daiwei Zhang, Wenxuan Song, Wei Huang, Lorenz Hurni
arxiv-2411-06971.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xue Xia, Daiwei Zhang, Wenxuan Song, Wei Huang, Lorenz Hurni. Automated feature detection in historical maps can significantly accelerate the reconstruction of the geospatial past. However, this process is often constrained by the time-consuming task of manually digitizing sufficient high-quality training data. The emergence of visual foundation models, such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM), offers a promising solution due to their remarkable generalization capabilities and rapid adaptation to new data distributions.

arxiv-2504-10926.title: RedDots: Planetary masses in the GJ1061 system from planet-planet interaction Thanks: Based on observations carried out at the European Southern Observatory under ESO programme 072.C-0488(E), 0101.C-0516(A), 198.C-0838(A), 1102.C-0339(A), and 183.C-0437(A)
arxiv-2504-10926.creator: S. Dreizler, S. V. Jeffers, F. Liebing, P. Gorrini, C. A. Haswell, E. Gaidos , {}^{{\ref{inst:hawaii},\ref{inst:vienna}}}, J. R. Barnes, F. Del Sordo , , {}^{{\ref{inst:ice},\ref{inst:ieec},\ref{inst:inaf}}}, H. R. A. Jones, E. Rodríguez, Y. Tsapras
arxiv-2504-10926.description: Abstract GJ 1061 is a very nearby M star hosting three low-mass temperate planets detected from radial velocity variations. The close to 4:2:1 period commensurability of the planets, the available long-term monitoring of the system and new very high-precision radial velocity measurements from ESPRESSO enable the determination of masses from the planet-planet interaction.

arxiv-2505-03646.title: Revealing Hidden Vulnerabilities in Autoencoders through Gradient Signal Restoration
arxiv-2505-03646.creator: Chethan Krishnamurthy Ramanaik, Arjun Roy, Tobias Callies, Eirini Ntoutsi
arxiv-2505-03646.description: Abstract . Adversarial robustness of deep autoencoders (AEs) has received less attention than that of discriminative models, although their compressed latent representations induce ill-conditioned mappings that can amplify small input perturbations and destabilize reconstructions. Existing white-box attacks for AEs, which optimize norm-bounded adversarial perturbations to maximize reconstruction damage, often converge to suboptimal perturbations, thereby potentially overstating AE robustness.

arxiv-2508-18849.title: Designing Antiferromagnetic Spin-1/2 Chains in Janus Fullerene Nanoribbons
arxiv-2508-18849.creator: Bo Peng, Michele Pizzochero
arxiv-2508-18849.description: Abstract We computationally design antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 chains in fullerene nanoribbons by introducing extra C 60 cages at one of their edges. The resulting odd number of intermolecular bonds induces an unpaired π \pi -electron and hence a quantised magnetic moment in otherwise non-magnetic nanoribbons.

arxiv-2511-02884.title: Adaptive Internal Calibration for Temperature-Robust mmWave FMCW Radars Conference: Companion of the the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing; October 12–16, 2025; Espoo, Finland Companion of the the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ub
arxiv-2511-02884.creator: Dariush Salami, Nima Bahmani, Hüseyin Yiğitler, Stephan Sigg
arxiv-2511-02884.description: Abstract . We present a novel internal calibration framework for Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) radars to ensure robust performance under internal temperature variations, tailored for deployment in dense wireless networks. Our approach mitigates the impact of temperature-induced drifts in radar hardware, enhancing reliability.

pmc-11293172.title: Development and validation of betel-year: a clinical tool for quantifying exposure to betel quid chewing, utilizing nuclear morphometric analysis and validated by cytomorphological analysis
pmc-11293172.creator: Hamrish Kumar Rajakumar, Varsha Coimbatore Sathyabal, Kolsamma Nasrin Jabarulla, Pushpa Balamurugesan
pmc-11293172.description: BackgroundBetel quid chewing, prevalent in Southeast Asia and South Asia, involves components such as betel leaf, areca nut, slaked lime, and sometimes tobacco. This study aims to assess buccal mucosa changes in betel quid chewers, develop a clinical tool for assessing exposure, and investigate its usability in predicting dysplasia.

pmc-11356222.title: Ionic Twin Nanostructural Comparison: Propylammonium Butanoate vs. Butylammonium Propanoate and Their Interactions with Water
pmc-11356222.creator: Umme Salma, Natalia V. Plechkova, Lorenzo Gontrani, Marilena Carbone
pmc-11356222.description: This study investigates the nanostructure of two protic ionic liquids (PILs), [N0 0 0 3][C3CO2] and [N0 0 0 4][C2CO2], with similar polar head groups but varying alkyl chain lengths. An X-ray scattering technique and molecular dynamics simulations have been utilized to characterize the bulk and interfacial properties of these PILs.

pmc-11456270.creator: Mariam Heikal, Halim Saad, Pia Maria Ghanime, Tarek Bou Dargham, Maya Bizri, Firas Kobeissy, Wassim El Hajj, Farid Talih
pmc-11456270.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveDelirium is a common and acute neuropsychiatric syndrome that requires timely intervention to prevent its associated morbidity and mortality. Yet, its diagnosis and symptoms are often overlooked due to its variable clinical presentation and fluctuating nature.

pmc-11500186.title: Soluble form of Lingo2, an autism spectrum disorder-associated molecule, functions as an excitatory synapse organizer in neurons
pmc-11500186.creator: Fumiaki Yoshida, Ryota Nagatomo, Shun Utsunomiya, Misaki Kimura, Shiyori Shun, Rena Kono, Yuma Kato, Yosuke Nao, Kazuma Maeda, Ryuta Koyama, Yuji Ikegaya, Stefan F. Lichtenthaler, Sho Takatori, Hiroshi Takemoto, Koichi Ogawa, Genta Ito, Taisuke Tomita
pmc-11500186.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder characterized by impaired social communication and repetitive behaviors. In recent years, a pharmacological mouse model of ASD involving maternal administration of valproic acid (VPA) has become widely used. Newborn pups in this model show an abnormal balance between excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) signaling in neurons and exhibit ASD-like behavior.

pmc-11591108.title: Identification of Recombinant Aichivirus D in Cattle, Italy
pmc-11591108.creator: Francesco Pellegrini, Gianvito Lanave, Francesca Caringella, Georgia Diakoudi, Anna Salvaggiulo, Alessandra Cavalli, Alessandro Papaleo, Barbara Di Martino, Michele Camero, Krisztián Bányai, Jelle Matthijnssens, Vito Martella
pmc-11591108.description: Simple SummaryKobuviruses (KoVs) possess a wide host range and have been associated with enteric disease in several host species. On screening of 38 stool samples collected from healthy (n = 21) and diarrheic (n = 17) animals, using a pan-KoV RT-PCR, viral RNA was detected in 10/38 (26.3%) samples.

pmc-11688190.title: PCAT19: the role in cancer pathogenesis and beyond
pmc-11688190.creator: Haijun Hu, Hongliang Luo, Ziqing Deng
pmc-11688190.description: PCAT19, a long non-coding RNA, has attracted considerable attention due to its diverse roles in various malignancies. This work compiles current research on PCAT19’s involvement in cancer pathogenesis and progression. Abnormal expression of PCAT19 has been observed in various cancers, and its correlation with clinical features and prognosis positions it as a promising prognostic biomarker.

pmc-12581348.title: Childhood trauma exposure, working memory updating, and exercise experience in adolescents with major depressive disorder
pmc-12581348.creator: Zhe Li, Junfeng Qin, Xianyun Zhu, Yinglin Wang, Wenxin Zhang, Donghui Shen, Xiaolei Xu
pmc-12581348.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIncreasing evidence indicates that childhood trauma (CT) experiences and impaired working memory updating (WMU) are critical factors in the development and maintenance of depression. Conversely, exercise activities serve as protective mechanisms against depression.

pmc-13116402.title: Destructive Mold Osteomyelitis of the Wrist Caused by Scedosporium apiospermum—A Case Report
pmc-13116402.creator: Camilla Bo, Anna Conen, Martina Giacalone, Regula Marti, Rainer Grobholz, Harald Seeger, Holger J. Klein, Jan A. Plock, Florian S. Frueh
pmc-13116402.description: Background: Wrist osteomyelitis caused by Scedosporium apiospermum is exceedingly rare. Its indolent course and destructive potential may result in extensive bone loss and pose substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Methods: We report a case of chronic wrist osteomyelitis caused by Scedosporium apiospermum in a 68-year-old kidney–pancreas transplant recipient.

pmc-13528414.title: Changes in hematological indices during adalimumab therapy in ankylosing spondylitis: a one-year retrospective study
pmc-13528414.creator: Dominika Szlichta, Magdalena Dryglewska, Ewa Łyś-Toporowska, Maria Majdan
pmc-13528414.description: IntroductionAnkylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease that can be managed with tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors. This study evaluated the effects of adalimumab, a TNF inhibitor, on inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Monitoring disease activity during therapy is important for assessing treatment response.
